LESSON: GUIDED WRITING: WRITING STYLES

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ARABIC LANGUAGE
Strand: Writing
Topic 3.2: Guided Writing: Writing Styles

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Guided Writing: Writing Styles. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How can you develop a good handwriting?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. write short paragraphs using appropriate signs (harakat)
2. appreciate use of signs appropriately in Arabic writing

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: GUIDED WRITING: WRITING STYLES
Subject: ARABIC LANGUAGE · Grade: Grade 6
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Guided Writing: Writing Styles helps you succeed in ARABIC LANGUAGE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: GUIDED WRITING: WRITING STYLES
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Write short paragraphs using appropriate signs (harakat)

What this means
In this part you learn to write short paragraphs using appropriate signs (harakat). You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: write short paragraphs using appropriate signs (harakat).
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Guided Writing: Writing Styles”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can write short paragraphs using appropriate signs (harakat). Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Appreciate use of signs appropriately in Arabic writing

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate use of signs appropriately in Arabic writing. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate use of signs appropriately in Arabic writing.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Guided Writing: Writing Styles to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate use of signs appropriately in Arabic writing. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Guided Writing: Writing Styles is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Guided Writing: Writing Styles”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: write short paragraphs using appropriate signs (harakat))

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Guided Writing: Writing Styles to a partner. (skill: appreciate use of signs appropriately in Arabic writing)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Guided Writing: Writing Styles to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: write short paragraphs using appropriate signs (harakat).
3. Practise this skill: appreciate use of signs appropriately in Arabic writing.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Guided Writing: Writing Styles from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Guided Writing: Writing Styles: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 6 learner study Guided Writing: Writing Styles?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can you develop a good handwriting?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Guided Writing: Writing Styles means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: write short paragraphs using appropriate signs (harakat).
5. Be able to: appreciate use of signs appropriately in Arabic writing.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
